function: Channel estimation in the delay-Doppler-angular domain: PositionNet+ recovers the sparse channel support and SSRnet recovers its values for massive MIMO-OTFS (pp. 1, 6-9).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OTFS, BS with Nt=1-64 antennas, single-antenna user, no RIS; fc=2.5 GHz (sub-6 GHz), M=600, N=10, 15 kHz spacing, 30-580 km/h (p. 10, Table II).
method: PositionNet+ (2D/3D CNN support finder) and SSRnet (adds deep-unfolded Learned ISP, 10 layers, and a 3D CNN denoiser); supervised learning, cosine/cross-entropy and log-NMSE losses (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: 3GPP spatial channel model, urban macrocell (MATLAB, TR 25.996, ref. [34]): 10^5 samples, 80% training and 20% validation; separate 10^3 realizations for testing (pp. 10, 13).
test_conditions: Training: SNR 0/10/20 dB (Fig. 7), Np=6 paths (Fig. 8), velocities 50/100/150 m/s (Fig. 11); testing: SNR 0-25 dB, Np=4 to 8, velocities 10-160 m/s (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: impulse-based estimation, OMP, 3D-SOMP, LS with perfect support, OFDM under ICI; learned: PositionNet [32], earlier work of the same authors, for support accuracy only (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Support accuracy, NMSE, uncoded BER with BPSK, pilot overhead ratio, CPU run time (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Table I complexity orders vs OMP and SBL; SSRnet has 2M_tau^2 N_nu^2 N_t + 490,700 parameters (p. 9); CPU run time 76.8% lower than 3D-SOMP (Fig. 14, p. 12).
openness: Simulation code at https://github.com/MostafaPayami/SSRnet (p. 10, reference [45] on p. 14).
q1_support: p. 10: "generated using the 3GPP spatial channel model in MATLAB" for training and testing data; reference [34] (p. 13) is the MATLAB implementation of the 3GPP Spatial Channel Model (TR 25.996), not TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 10: "trained only with Np = 6 paths" and tested with other numbers of paths (Fig. 8); p. 11: "the network was trained for user velocities of {50, 100, 150} m/s", tested from 10 to 160 m/s (Fig. 11).
q3_support: p. 10: "more accurate in finding the support of the desired sparse channel matrix than that of OMP, 3D-SOMP [17] as well as the recently proposed PositionNet [32]"; the NMSE and BER comparisons of SSRnet (pp. 11-12) use only non-learned baselines.
q4_support: p. 9: "the proposed SSRnet has a lower complexity order compared with OMP and SBL algorithms" (Table I, parameter count); p. 12: "a significant computation time reduction of 76.8% is achieved compared to that of the 3D-SOMP algorithm".
q5_support: p. 10: "Simulation codes for the experimental results are available online at the repository [45]"; p. 14: reference [45] gives https://github.com/MostafaPayami/SSRnet.
notes: Included, area 4: channel estimation in the delay-Doppler domain of MIMO-OTFS (area 4 wins over area 2). PDF is the paper of the DOI (title and DOI on p. 1). q1 rests on the 3GPP spatial channel model of TR 25.996 (p. 10, ref. [34] on p. 13), another standardized model, for the reviewer to confirm. q3 rests on PositionNet+ vs PositionNet [32] and OMP/3D-SOMP in support accuracy (Figs. 7-8, p. 10); SSRnet is compared on NMSE and BER with non-learned methods only (Figs. 9-13). q2 counts the Np and velocity mismatch, not the SNR, antenna or overhead sweeps. Table I, Table II and Figs. 7-14 were read as page images.
